humanities_role_explanation: LongFact spans 38 topics (STEM, social sciences, humanities, other); humanities topics (history, philosophy, music, world religions, architecture) only supply open-domain subject matter for a generic long-form factuality test. The competence tested is general factual precision/recall, not disciplinary interpretation.
benchmark_modalities_explanation: Text-only prompts and long-form text responses, evaluated claim-by-claim against Google Search results.
analytical_tasks_explanation: Models answer fact-seeking prompts with long-form responses (open-ended QA/generation). Responses are decomposed into atomic facts (information extraction) and each is rated supported/not supported/irrelevant via search (fact verification). Paper's terms: long-form factuality, F1@K, precision and recall of supported facts.

general_purpose_benchmark.note: Broad multi-topic prompt set across 38 topics in open domains.

evaluates_generative_llm.note: Thirteen models: Gemini-Ultra/Pro, GPT-4-Turbo/GPT-4/GPT-3.5-Turbo, Claude-3 Opus/Sonnet/Haiku, Claude-2.1/2.0/Instant, PaLM-2-L-IT(-RLHF).

quantitative_metrics.note: F1@K (K=64, 178), precision, recall, counts of supported/not-supported facts; SAFE-human agreement.

summary: The paper introduces LongFact, a GPT-4-generated set of 2,280 long-form fact-seeking prompts across 38 topics, SAFE, a search-augmented LLM fact-checking agent, and F1@K, a metric combining factual precision with recall relative to a preferred length K. It benchmarks thirteen LLMs and shows SAFE outperforms crowdsourced annotators on disagreements at far lower cost.
key_findings: SAFE agrees with 72.0% of 16,011 crowdsourced fact labels and wins 76% of 100 disagreement cases (humans 19%), at over 20x lower cost. Larger models are generally more factual; GPT-4-Turbo scores highest (F1@64 95.0, F1@178 66.4).
evaluation_unit: prompt (LongFact prompt with long-form model response, rated at the level of individual facts)
facets_explanation: LongFact prompts were generated by GPT-4 from manually chosen topics and exemplars, then manually deduplicated. There is no fixed answer key: each atomic fact in a model response is judged by an LLM agent (SAFE) against Google Search results, so correctness depends on external knowledge. The paper treats controversial facts by majority vote of available information, but does not discuss disagreement between readings.
results_explanation: Table 2 reports GPT-4-Turbo with F1@64 95.0 and F1@178 66.4 (the headline is F1@K, mapped to 'other'). Comparisons on the same models include LongFact-Concepts being easier than LongFact-Objects and the postamble lowering precision, but no numeric gap in points is stated in the text, so reported_format_gap_points is null. The SAFE-vs-crowd comparison (72.0% agreement; SAFE 76% vs human 19% on disagreements) is an annotator comparison, not a human baseline for model scores.

humanities_role.quote: LongFact consists of 38 topics (listed in Appendix B.2) categorized into four supercategories.

dataset_size.quote: LongFact consists of 2,280 fact-seeking prompts that solicit long-form responses across 38 manually-selected topics.

evaluation_set_size.quote: We evaluate each model on the same random subset of 250 prompts

primary_evaluation_setting.quote: we decode model responses up to 1,024 tokens at a temperature of zero

gold_source.quote: We use GPT-4 to generate a new prompt set for benchmarking long-form factuality in large language models

gold_beyond_stimulus.quote: Google Search can be leveraged to obtain dynamic reference answers for each fact in a response

reported_format_gap.quote: model responses on LongFact-Concepts have better long-form factuality than model responses on LongFact-Objects for all K and on all three benchmarked models

reported_format_gap_kind.quote: LongFact-Concepts is an easier prompt set than LongFact-Objects
